chunks: 3257 - And ʿAlī عليه السلام judged regarding a man whom two men brought and said: “This man stole a coat of armor.” The man began imploring him when he examined the evidence, and he kept saying: “By Allah, if the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله were present, he would never cut off my hand.” He said: “And why?” He said: “My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, would inform him that I am innocent, and so he would declare me innocent through my innocence.”

So when ʿAlī عليه السلام saw his imploring him, he called the two witnesses and said to them: “Fear Allah, and do not cut the man’s hand unjustly.” And he adjured them, then said: “Let one of you cut off his hand and let the other hold his hand.”

Then when they went forward to the platform to cut off his hand, they struck at the people until they became mixed together. Then when they had become mixed together, they let the man go into the midst of the people, and the two fled until they blended in with the people.

Then the man against whom they had testified came and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the two men testified against me unjustly. When they struck the people and they became mixed together, they let me go and fled. Had they been truthful, they would neither have fled nor released me.” So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Who will direct me to these two witnesses so that I may punish them?”

key_terms.أُنَكِّلْهُمَا: I will punish them as a deterrent
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةِ: the evidentiary proof examined in the case
key_terms.الْمِصْطَبَّةِ: the raised platform to which they advanced

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام deal with false witnesses in a theft case?
ai.summary: This report recounts a judicial case in which Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام dealt carefully with testimony in an accusation of theft. The conduct of the two witnesses exposed their falsehood, and the Imam sought to punish them for their unjust testimony, highlighting justice, caution in hudud-related claims, and accountability for false witness.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3257 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) judged in the case of a man who was brought by two others who said: "This man has stolen a coat of armor."
The accused pleaded with Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) to examine the evidence carefully and said: "By Allah (swt), if the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) were here, he would never cut off my hand."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) asked: "Why?"
The man replied: "Because my Lord (azj), the Almighty, would have informed him of my innocence, and He (sw) would have declared me innocent based on that knowledge."

When Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) saw how the man pleaded, Imam (as) called the two witnesses and said to them: "Fear Allah (swt), and do not have this man's hand cut off unjustly."
Imam (as) continued to appeal to them and then said: "Let one of you cut off his hand while the other holds it."

As they prepared to execute the sentence, they stirred the people, causing a commotion in the crowd.
In the chaos, they released the accused man and fled, blending into the crowd.

The accused man then returned and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, these two men testified against me falsely. When the crowd was stirred, they released me and fled. If they were truthful, they would neither have fled nor let me go."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "Who can lead me to these two witnesses so that I may punish them?"
